chunks: And from him from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who hunted while he was in the state of Ihram, and his hand or leg was broken, so the game continued on its way, and the man did not know what happened to the game. He said: 'He must pay the full compensation if he does not know what happened to the game.'
If he saw it after his hand or leg was broken, and it had grazed and recovered, then one-quarter of its value is upon him. Narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فِدَاء: Compensation or ransom paid for a religious obligation or transgression

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on compensation for accidental hunting while in Ihram if the hunter's limb is broken?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies the variable nature of fidyah based on the hunter's knowledge of the game's fate, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that liability often hinges on awareness and actual loss. It highlights the practical application of proportional compensation in Hajj rituals, distinguishing between total loss (full value) and partial recovery (one-quarter value). This ruling underscores the balance between strict adherence to Ihram conditions and fairness in assessing the extent of the transgression.
